subject: POC trial planning: traffic profile & success criteria (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC trial planning: traffic profile & success criteria (Acme Health)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled: 

Recap (from our call):
- Goal: Validate Redwood can meet Acme Health's interactive assistant latency and cost targets for the triage workflow (clinical intake -> triage notes).
- Primary success criteria discussed: 95th percentile latency < 400ms for single-turn interactions at production-like concurrency, throughput to support 150 RPS sustained during business hours, and <10% relative degradation in model output quality vs your current baseline prompts.
- Data: You’ll provide a representative traffic sample and token-length distribution; we’ll run a 2-week trial with a synthetic traffic replay and a 1-week live shadow run (if you want).

Ask: Can you send the workload profile we discussed (RPS by hour, token length distribution, concurrency, burst patterns) and any baseline cost/latency numbers you have? A CSV sample (timestamped requests + avg tokens) is ideal.

Proposed POC/Eval plan (high level):
1) Intake (this week): receive traffic sample + success criteria signoff (you)
2) Config & baseline (wk 1): Redwood config + synthetic replay to measure baseline throughput/latency
3) Live shadow (optional wk 2): short live traffic window for end-to-end validation
4) Results & next steps: handoff to SRE/Infra for production plan or reserved capacity quote

Owners: Ben (Sales/Coordination), Marissa (POC execution lead), Dylan (SRE/infra for perf tuning).

Timeline: If we get the sample by Wed 3/31, we can start the baseline run the week of 4/6 and aim to wrap by 4/17.

Attachments: I’ll attach a sample CSV template (acme_health_traffic_profile.csv) — please populate with one week of representative requests if possible.

Next steps:
- Alex / Priya: send workload sample + confirm the three success criteria above or suggest edits.
- We’ll confirm POC dates after intake.

Thanks,
Ben

Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the recap and the template. Attached is a first-pass traffic sample (acme_health_traffic_profile.csv). Notes / clarifications below: 

What’s in the CSV: one week of production logs (sampled) with timestamp, request_type, user_id hash, avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens, and observed_latency_ms (our current stack).

Key numbers (summary):
- Typical sustained RPS (business hours 8am-6pm ET): 75 RPS
- Peak sustained RPS (10–11am ET): 150 RPS for ~20 mins
- Burst behavior: short spikes up to ~300 RPS lasting 30–90 seconds (eg, morning batch releases & triage surges)
- Average request token lengths: input ~120 tokens, output ~80 tokens; 95th percentile input ~420 tokens
- Concurrency: our frontend shows ~120 concurrent open sessions during peak minutes (these generate parallel requests)

Success criteria feedback: 
- 95th percentile latency < 400ms is reasonable for single-turn inference. We’d like to add stability: error rate (5xx or timeouts) < 0.5% during peak sustained periods.
- For quality, we’ll share a small prompt set (50 queries) to evaluate hallucination rate and clinical relevance vs current baseline.

Attachments: acme_health_traffic_profile.csv (sample)

Let us know if you need additional fields (payload size, tokenizer used, etc.). Happy to hop on a quick tech-sync with your SREs if it helps.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Product
Acme Health
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: POC trial planning: traffic profile & success criteria (Acme Health)

Alex / Priya —

Got the CSV (thanks) — this is exactly what we needed. Quick response with the proposed evaluation plan updated for your numbers: 

Updated POC scope (2-week plan):
- Week 0 (Intake & config): Confirm tokens/encoding, ingest CSV, synthetic replay config. Marissa to provision a sandbox environment and baseline model variant.
- Week 1 (Baseline replay): Run synthetic replay targeting your reported sustained 75 RPS, ramp to 150 RPS for short windows, and inject burst patterns to 300 RPS. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, success criteria & error rates. Dylan to run perf tuning and submit a quantized model variant test if needed.
- Week 2 (Live shadow — optional): If you opt in, route a small % of live traffic to Redwood in shadow mode for end-to-end validation. This helps catch integration / tokenization edge cases.

Concrete success criteria for the report we’ll deliver:
- Performance: p95 latency < 400ms at 150 RPS sustained; system stable (error rate < 0.5%) under sustained peak and during short bursts.
- Quality: For your 50-query eval set, output quality (clinician relevance + hallucination rate) not worse than baseline by more than 10% absolute (we'll agree measurement rubric).
- Cost: Estimated per-1M-token serving cost and suggested reserved capacity configuration for target SLAs.

Ownership:
- Acme: sign off success criteria + provide eval prompt set and live shadow approval (if needed).
- Redwood: Marissa (POC lead) executes runs and produces results; Dylan handles infra tuning; Ben coordinates commercial follow-ups (pricing/reserved capacity).

Logistics / timeline:
- Marissa will reach out to schedule a 30-min tech sync with Dylan and your infra lead (Priya?) to confirm tokenization and any integration details.
- Tentative baseline run: week of 4/6; report out by 4/17.

Links / next steps:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2026-001
- Please confirm: 1) success criteria above, 2) whether you want the optional live shadow in week 2, 3) who from Acme will join the tech sync (Priya? infra lead?).

We’ll also prepare an initial reserved-capacity estimate based on the traffic profile — Ben will send that in a separate note.

Thanks — look forward to getting this scheduled.

Ben
